design_reference: No dedicated wireframe screen — cloud-sync is infrastructure. Its only UI surface is a small sync-status affordance (online/offline/syncing/conflict) rendered with design-system tokens (a muted Badge in the top bar of tree-canvas / book-library). Keep it quiet and low-fi; tokens from styles.css.

plan.goal: Provide cloud-first persistence for books: local writes are the source of truth and always succeed; changes sync to the cloud in the background; conflicts are detected and resolved without losing an author's work. Owns CloudSyncService in brain.

design_contract._binding: Minimal, quiet UI only. A sync-status `Badge` (muted/neutral; accent when syncing; bad tone on conflict) sits in the existing top bars. No full sync dashboard, no blocking spinners over the editor. Tokens from styles.css.
design_contract.status_states: idle/synced (muted ✓), syncing (accent ↻), offline (muted, « hors ligne — modifications locales »), conflict (bad tone, opens a minimal resolution affordance).
design_contract.non_goal_ui: Sync must never block authoring: no modal spinners gating edits; status is ambient.

acceptance_criteria: All persistence flows through PersistenceService locally; CloudSyncService layers background push/pull on top — a write succeeds locally and is observable immediately even with no network (cloud-first).
When offline, edits are queued and the status shows « hors ligne »; on reconnect the queue flushes in order and the status returns to synced, with no lost or duplicated writes.
CloudSyncService exposes a subscribable status (idle/syncing/offline/conflict) and emits sync:status{state}; the top-bar Badge reflects it without polling.

Concurrent edits to the same book from two clients are detected via per-document version/clock; a conflict is surfaced (sync:status 'conflict') and resolved by a defined strategy (last-write-wins per field with a recoverable backup, or a minimal pick-a-side) — never a silent overwrite of the larger/older document.
The save-shrink safeguard holds: a sync pull must not replace a local book with a drastically smaller/empty remote unless that deletion is explicitly intended (guards accidental data loss).
Book ids are the stable sync keys; the seeded tree (Sommaire + isolated Mort) round-trips through sync intact (node/edge counts preserved).
Sensitive sync material (tokens) is kept out of the synced document and flagged in persistenceKeys.ts; nothing secret is written into book data.
The status affordance renders from design-system tokens, light theme, and never blocks authoring (no edit-gating spinner).
plan.walking_skeleton: Wrap PersistenceService with CloudSyncService: local write-through (always succeeds) + a background push to the cloud store; on load, pull remote and merge into local. Expose a status + emit sync:status; render the top-bar Badge. Defer real conflict UI — start with last-write-wins + a backup. Prove the offline-queue + reconnect-flush path end-to-end.

iterations.goal: Local write-through + background push/pull: CloudSyncService over PersistenceService; books load local-first then reconcile remote without flicker; status + sync:status + top-bar Badge. Design-system fidelity on the badge.
Offline queue + reconnect flush: queue writes offline, flush in order on reconnect, no loss/dup; « hors ligne » status; integrate with book-creation's offline-create path (KR-005).

Conflict detection + safe resolution: per-document version/clock, conflict status, defined resolution (LWW-per-field + recoverable backup or minimal pick-a-side), shrink-guard against destructive remote pulls (KR-122).

known_risks: KR-120 — Cloud-first inversion: the LOCAL store is the source of truth; the cloud is a background replica. A naive 'cloud wins' pull will clobber unsynced local edits. Local write-through must always succeed and never be gated on the network (re-asserts KR-005).
KR-121 — Ordering + dedupe: the offline queue must flush in causal order and be idempotent so a retried push doesn't duplicate nodes/edges or resurrect deleted books.

KR-122 — Destructive-pull guard: never replace a local book with a drastically smaller/empty remote document unless the deletion is explicit (mirrors the >50% shrink safeguard); a bad pull can wipe an author's book.
KR-123 — Conflict resolution must be recoverable: keep a backup of the losing side; silent last-write-wins that discards the other client's work is unacceptable for long-form authoring.
KR-124 — Sync must not block authoring: no edit-gating spinners; status is ambient. Coupling the editor's responsiveness to network latency makes the tool feel broken offline.
KR-011 — Persistence only via PersistenceService/persistenceKeys.ts; no raw localStorage anywhere (global config KR-111).
KR-125 — Secrets (sync tokens) never go into the synced book document; keep them in a SENSITIVE-flagged key (config hygiene).
A11y — the status badge has an accessible label conveying state; conflict resolution (if any UI) is keyboard-operable.

resolved_decisions: Cloud-first: local is the source of truth; sync is background; authoring never blocks on the network (per the brain proposal the user validated).
UI is a quiet ambient status badge only — no sync dashboard.
Sync keys are book ids; secrets stay out of the synced document.
open_questions: Cloud backend: confirm the Cloudflare Worker + store assumption from the brain proposal, and the document granularity (whole-book vs per-node sync).
Conflict strategy default: last-write-wins-per-field with backup vs explicit pick-a-side — leaning LWW-per-field + recoverable backup.
